catalog_quote: Pichi is a tone language. In previous work, I posited that Pichi has a mixed prosodic system in which individual words are either specified for pitch accent or tone (Yakpo 2009a,c)... I found no evidence that the Pichi lexicon is stratified and that “tonal” and “pitch-accented” words differ with respect to their pitch-related properties or the tonal processes described in this chapter. I therefore treat the prosodic system of Pichi as a tonal system tout court. ... Pichi has two distinctive tonemes, namely a High (H) and a Low (L) tone. The language employs lexical and morphological tone, and there is an unevenly distributed number of tone classes. ... About 95 per cent of roots contained in my lexical data-base carry a single H tone over their only, penultimate, or final syllable. Other syllables in these words are L-toned. ... audit.reasoning: The classification (tonal; no word stress; H/L lexical and morphological tone; single-H position lexically specified as a residue of stress-to-tone conversion) rests on the 2019 open-access LSP reference grammar by the language's principal describer, which we hold; every fragment of the deciding quotation and the domain quotation was found verbatim at the stated pages (37, 45, 55), and the the primary-stress rule's percentages match Table 3.2 (p. 46). Glottolog offers nothing better (older versions of the same grammar, an APiCS sketch, 1919/1938 colonial sketches). the one later prosody article found (Bordal Steien & Yakpo 2020, Language) was downloaded to and confirms the classification on pp. 10-11. no reclassification or re-read ne

sources.quote: 'Pichi has two phonological tones, a level H and a level L tone. The language features numerous monosyllabic tonal minimal pairs ... Grammatical tone is used for the inflection of personal pronouns for case and in compounding ... Most English-derived words ... bear at least and not more than one H, and the position of the H tone largely coincides with primary stress placement in the cognate forms of English.' and 'In Sango and Pichi, tones are exponents of morphemes ...
